checks.what: IV-1: 1390 ppm of carbon dioxide at 100.0 kPa is 1.04 mmHg; the table says 1.03
V-2: 2360 ppm of carbon dioxide at 70.7 kPa is 1.25 mmHg; the table says 1.26
VI-2: 2800 ppm of carbon dioxide at 54.1 kPa is 1.14 mmHg; the table says 1.15
VI-3: 8539 ppm of carbon dioxide at 54.6 kPa is 3.50 mmHg; the table says 3.51
VI-4: 8117 ppm of carbon dioxide at 55.2 kPa is 3.36 mmHg; the table says 3.37
the paper says both PMMA tests exceeded the carbon dioxide limit of 3 mmHg: the table gives 3.51 and 3.37
the paper says their carbon monoxide was above the 24-hour limit of 100 ppm and close to the 1-hour limit of 425: the table gives 308 and 320
one row of the table has all ten values, which fixes the order of the columns (VI-2)

saffire.not_used: Table 2 also lists burn duration and heat release. Some of those cells are empty, and the stored text does not show which, so they are left out.

fm2.title: The four tests planned on the Moon (FM2)

ref.source: Ferkul et al., Material Flammability at Lunar and Martian Gravity, presentation, NTRS 20260001966

checks.what: four tests, each at the same pressure, in falling order of oxygen

saffire.quote: Selecting 1 mg/m3 as a relatively tight alarm threshold, the FFD detector reached that threshold at 981 seconds. By this point, much of the hazardous gas release had occurred.
saffire.says: The two-sided acrylic sample of Saffire VI
saffire.source: Urban et al., Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment, ICES-2024-365, NTRS 20240002981

saffire.quote: Despite these fires, the temperature only increased significantly very near to the fire itself.
saffire.source: Urban et al., Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment, ICES-2024-365, NTRS 20240002981

saffire.quote: the human hazard from a fire in a spacecraft is very similar to terrestrial fires where the heat from the fire is not the principal hazard and rather the smoke and gaseous products are a much greater concern
saffire.source: Urban et al., Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment, ICES-2024-365, NTRS 20240002981

saffire.quote: Further work will be needed to extend these results to the partial gravity environment expected on future mission to the moon and Mars.
saffire.source: Urban et al., Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment, ICES-2024-365, NTRS 20240002981

luci.quote: Two samples are burned simultaneously in air at normal pressure
luci.source: Ferkul et al., Lunar Combustion Investigation: Flammability Results from a Rotating Sounding Rocket, presentation, NTRS 20250010653

luci.quote: 1-g extinction happens ~ 45 seconds sooner than partial-g extinction
luci.says: The fabric burned longer in lunar gravity
luci.source: Ferkul et al., Lunar Combustion Investigation: Flammability Results from a Rotating Sounding Rocket, presentation, NTRS 20250010653

luci.quote: Flame extinction for 1-g experiment occurs quicker
luci.source: Ferkul et al., Lunar Combustion Investigation: Flammability Results from a Rotating Sounding Rocket, presentation, NTRS 20250010653

luci.quote: demonstrates how the Coriolis force pulls the flame away from the axis of the fuel
luci.source: Ferkul et al., Lunar Combustion Investigation: Flammability Results from a Rotating Sounding Rocket, presentation, NTRS 20250010653

luci.quote: Material flammability testing at partial-g is feasible using a spinning vehicle.
luci.source: Ferkul et al., Lunar Combustion Investigation: Flammability Results from a Rotating Sounding Rocket, presentation, NTRS 20250010653

lunar.quote: the crucial mechanism of buoyant oxygen entrainment at the flame base is still present, but at a slower rate
lunar.says: Why a fire on the Moon does not wait for a fan
lunar.source: Ferkul, Kralik and Liao, Material Flammability at Lunar and Martian Gravity, extended abstract, NTRS 20260000646

lunar.quote: partial-g fire in an extraterrestrial habitat is a real hazard that is expected to be substantially worse than in 0-g and potentially worse than even 1-g
lunar.source: Ferkul, Kralik and Liao, Material Flammability at Lunar and Martian Gravity, extended abstract, NTRS 20260000646

lunar.quote: Related work suggests that oxygen concentration for flammability reaches a minimum value in the vicinity of g = g Lunar.
lunar.source: Ferkul, Kralik and Liao, Material Flammability at Lunar and Martian Gravity, extended abstract, NTRS 20260000646

lunar.quote: the available times are too short to provide significant flame development (5 s for drop tower and ~25 s for aircraft)
lunar.says: Why so little has been measured
lunar.source: Ferkul, Kralik and Liao, Material Flammability at Lunar and Martian Gravity, extended abstract, NTRS 20260000646

lunar.quote: The first-ever combustion experiments on another world will be performed, with a planned launch date of late 2026.
lunar.source: Ferkul, Kralik and Liao, Material Flammability at Lunar and Martian Gravity, extended abstract, NTRS 20260000646

fm2.quote: Four 20-cm tall fabric samples burned individually; atmosphere is refreshed between burns
fm2.source: Ferkul et al., Material Flammability at Lunar and Martian Gravity, presentation, NTRS 20260001966

fm2.quote: There is mounting evidence that if a material passes the NASA standard test it might fail at levels of gravity and flow below 1-g.
fm2.source: Ferkul et al., Material Flammability at Lunar and Martian Gravity, presentation, NTRS 20260001966

fm2.quote: not expected to ignite but would provide a margin of safety if the limit was lower than expected
fm2.source: Ferkul et al., Material Flammability at Lunar and Martian Gravity, presentation, NTRS 20260001966
